Mr. R.J. Shinde, Advocate for applicants.

Ms. Kiran P. Wathore, Advocate for non-applicant No.2.
 Coram : Urmila Joshi-Phalke And
 Nandesh S. Deshpande, Jj.
 Date : 03rd October, 2025.

1.  Present application is filed by the applicants   quashing of First Information Report in connection with Crime  No.48/2022, registered with Police Station Risod, District  Washim for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323,
 504 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The Crime is registered on the basis of report   by the informant on an allegation that her marriage is  performed with applicant No.1 on 14.5.2020.
After marriage  she resumed the cohabitation.
As per the allegations she was  not treated well on the count that the marriage was not  performed as per the status of the present applicants and othe  reasons.
3. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, who
submitted

that during the pendency of this application both  parties arrived at a settlement and it was decided that the  937-apl267.22.odt 2/4  marriage to be dissolved and permanent alimony of  Rs.3,00,000/- is paid to the non-applicant No.2.
He submitted  that the amount is already paid.
In view of that, the First Baliram Dnyanba Shelke And 6 Others vs The State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Risod ...

1  Information Report be quashed against the present applicants.

He further submitted that as the present applicants have not  appeared before this Court, therefore non-bailable warrant was  issued and the applicant No.1/Baliram Shelke and applicant  No.4/Santosh Shelke are already arrested by the Police in  execution of that warrant.
Therefore, they be released.
4. Learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application and  submitted that the recitals of the F.I.R. itself sufficient to show  prima facie material against the present applicants.
In view of  that, application deserves to be rejected.
5. Learned counsel for the complainant informant  admitted that the matter is settled and the informant has  received the amount towards permanent alimony.
The penalty  amount is also deposited by the present applicants by  depositing the same in her account.
6. The applicants and non-applicant No.2 both were  present before this Court on 23.9.2025.
The contents of the  settlement are verified from them.

They have accepted the  settlement, but as the applicants have not paid the amount,
 therefore, the matter was not disposed of on earlier occasion.
Now the compliance is already made, the amount of penalty is  also deposited by the present applicants.

In view of that, and  considering the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the  case Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another, reported in  MANU/SC/0781/2012, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court  observed that "Where the High Court quashes a criminal  937-apl267.22.odt 3/4  proceeding having regard to the fact that the dispute between  the offender and victim has been settled, although the offences  are not compoundable, it does so as in its opinion, continuation  of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice  in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is put  to an end and peace is restored; securing the ends of justice  being the ultimate guiding factor."

(iii) The applicant No.1/Baliram Shelke and applicant No.4/Santosh Shelke who are taken into the custody by executing the warrant be released forthwith.
